title: Photography
text:
As a wizard and scholar of Middle-earth, I have been studying the magic of the natural world for centuries. Through my self-portraits, I aim to capture the essence of my own being and reflect on my own journey through time. Each photograph is a reflection of my own experiences and emotions. Through my photography, I hope to offer a glimpse into my life as a scholar and adventurer, and inspire others to reflect on their own journeys through the world.

Over the centuries, I have devoted countless hours to deciphering and translating the ancient scripts and dialects of the various peoples of Middle-earth. My goal is to gain a deeper understanding of the cultures and histories of these peoples by studying their languages. Currently, I am working on a monograph that explores the linguistic roots of the Elvish languages. Through extensive research and analysis, I hope to shed light on the connections between the different dialects of Elvish and their origins. This project has been particularly challenging, as Elvish is a complex and nuanced language, but I am determined to see it through to completion.

The History of the War of the Ring

I am creating a comprehensive and detailed history of the conflict that goes beyond the surface-level events. By gathering information from a variety of sources, including my own memories, written accounts, and oral histories, I hope to shed new light on this important period in Middle-earth’s history and provide valuable insights into the motivations and actions of the various players involved.

Welcome to my website!
Hello! My name is Rachana Gurudu, and I am a combined bachelor’s/master’s student at Case Western Reserve University pursuing a B.A. in Chemical Biology, a B.A. in Healthcare Management and an M.S. in Biomedical and Health Informatics. I am passionate about interdiscplinary studies, and the intersection of medicine, equity, and technology. In the future, I aim to be a physician-researcher who develops informatics tools to solve pressing health equity issues and makes healthcare more accessible.
My research interests include the evaluation of leadership development programs for women faculty at CWRU School of Medicine, automated view classification tools of cardiac MR, and general radiology topics such as claustrophobia in MRI and tumor metrics imaging core labs. Outside of research, I am passionate about disability accessibility, and serve as President and Founder of the Disability Resources Student Advisory Board, where I advocate on a ten-person board to make CWRU’s campus and courses more accessible. Outside of research and extracurriculars, I am a long-distance runner, and plan to run a marathon next spring!
Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions or would like to discuss potential projects.

Leveraging Generative AI Tools to Track Long-Term Leadership Trajectories in Academic Medicine (Current)
Utilizing generative AI to assess efficacy of leadership development programs for women in academic medicine at CWRU School of Medicine Clinical and Translational Science Collaborative and CWRU Weatherhead School of Management.

title: Projects
section: Development and Validation of a Simplified Martin-Hopkins LDL-C Equation Using Machine Learning (2026)
text:
Development and Validation of a Simplified Martin-Hopkins LDL-C Equation Using Machine Learning (2026)
Validated a machine-learning based model to recalculate low density lipoprotein cholesterol to improve accuracy on Mayo Clinic laboratory data, and published findings in JAMA Cardiology.

title: Projects
section: Feasibility of Capillary Self-Collected Blood Specimens for Routine Outpatient Laboratory Testing (2026)
text:
Feasibility of Capillary Self-Collected Blood Specimens for Routine Outpatient Laboratory Testing (2026)
Evaluated the clinical efficacy and viability of at-home capillary blood collection device for outpatient diagnostic testing at Mayo Clinic. Presenting findings at the Association for Diagnostics & Laboratory Medicine Pre-Analytical Phase Conference, and published manuscript in the Journal of Applied Laboratory Medicine.

title: Projects
section: Tumor metrics imaging core labs: primer for radiologists (2026)
text:
Tumor metrics imaging core labs: primer for radiologists (2026)
First-authored a review paper discussing the role, importance, benefits, and costs of tumor metrics imaging core labs for oncological clinical trials. Published review in Abdominal Radiology.

title: Projects
section: Revisiting MRI Claustrophobia: Incidence, Factors, and Interventions, Journal of Computer Assisted Tomography (2025)
text:
Revisiting MRI Claustrophobia: Incidence, Factors, and Interventions, Journal of Computer Assisted Tomography (2025)
Assisted in writing a review paper encompassing claustrophobia in MRI imaging, including incidence, causes, and potential interventions. Published review in the Journal of Computer Assisted Tomography.

Patient-Reported Testing Burden of Screening Contrast Enhanced Mammography (2023)
Assessed the testing burden through patient-reported surveys of screening contrast-enhanced mammography for high-risk patients. Published results in the Journal of the American College of Radiology.
